newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil premiums firm, diesel eases.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil premiums firm, diesel eases.

text.p: Steady demand gave firm support to NWE heating oil premiums but ebbing inquiry shaved value from low sulphur diesel cargoes on Tuesday, traders said.
Benchmark February IPE gas oil futures closed down $5.25 at $203.75 a tonne with weaker NYMEX heating oil, ample supply and warmer U.S. and European temperatures.
Cargo and barge traders said volumes were thin, with activity depressed by expensive shipping and buyer reluctance in a falling screen market.

In cargoes, German winter grade heating oil traded unchanged at Feb IPE +$8.50 cif NWE. French heating oil traded at Feb IPE +14 cif Le Havre, the bullish number that was the focus of discussions for the past two days for the 20,000 tonne parcel.
Weakening demand pulled low sulphur diesel cargo premiums down $4. The material traded at Feb IPE +$16 cif NWE for the end of January.
Barges were thinly traded, with heating oil sliding $1.50 on meagre demand caused by ice that blocked canal deliveries.
Refinery grade heating oil traded at Feb +$6 and Feb +$6.50 prompt fob ARA. February was done at Feb +$4. Low sulphur diesel gained $1, with prompt material done at Feb +$13.50 fob ARA.
